promptLatex: Ten percent of the items coming off a production line are defective. Two items are taken at random from a large shipment. Given that at least one of them is defective, what is the probability that both are defective?
hintLatex: Compute the probability of the condition and the probability of the stronger event, then divide.
Both items being defective has probability $\left(\frac{1}{10}\right)^2 = \frac{1}{100}$.
At least one being defective is the complement of both being sound, namely $1 - \left(\frac{9}{10}\right)^2 = \frac{19}{100}$.
